Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each item of business referred to on the agenda are on file in the office of the City Clerk and are available for public inspection. If applicable, materials related to an item on this agenda submitted to the Council after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's office during normal business hours. Any person having any question concerning any agenda item may call the City Clerk to make inquiry concerning the item. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act. Please contact the City Clerk at 310-378-0383, at least 48 hours prior to the meeting to request a disability-related modification or accommodation.
The City Council welcomes and encourages public participation at the Council meetings; however, to allow for the orderly progression of business, each person wishing to comment or make a presentation shall be limited to up to three (3) minutes. Anyone wishing to address the City Council is requested to fill out a green speaker's card available at the entry of the meeting room. The card permits the City to identify persons for purposes of City Council minute preparation. Please see specific agenda sections below for any other requirements related to meeting participation. The City Council, at the direction of the Mayor with concurrence of the Council, may modify the order of items shown on the agenda.
This meeting will be held via video-conference only in order to reduce the risk of spreading COVID-19 and pursuant to the Governor's Executive Orders N-25-20 and N-29-20 and the County of Los Angeles Public Health Officer's Safer at Home Order (revised March 21, 2020). All votes taken during this teleconference meeting will be by roll call vote, and the vote will be publicly reported.
HOW TO VIEW THE MEETING: No physical location from which members of the public may
observe the meeting and offer public comment will be provided. The meeting will not be livestreamed. You may attend the meeting through a computer or telephone:
BY COMPUTER:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/86707734458
Zoom Meeting ID: 867 0773 4458 or
BY TELEPHONE: 1 669 900 9128, Enter Code 867 0773 4458#
HOW TO PARTICIPATE BEFORE THE MEETING: Members of the public are encouraged to submit email correspondence to CityCouncilMeeting@pvestates.org before the meeting begins. The email will be distributed to all councilmembers. Public correspondence submitted electronically via email will be provided to the legislative body, but will not be read aloud at the meeting.
HOW TO PARTICIPATE DURING THE MEETING: If you would like to address the City Council during the meeting, please email CityCouncilMeeting@pvestates.org by 5:00 p.m. on Tuesday, June 9th, with (1) your name, (2) the agenda item on which you'd like to speak, and (3) the phone number and/or Zoom name from which you will be calling in to the meeting.

MINUTES
  OF THE JUNE 9, 2020 REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  PALOS VERDES ESTATES, CALIFORNIA

NEXT RESOLUTION NO. R20-19

NEXT ORDINANCE NO. O20-745

A Teleconference meeting of the Palos Verdes Estates City Council meeting via Zoom pursuant to
Executive Order N25-20 issued by Governor Gavin Newsom on March 26, 2020, was called to order
by Mayor McGowan at 6:33 P.M. on June 9, 2020, notice having been given with affidavit thereto on
file. Members of the public were provided with the following information to provide public input:

  BY COMPUTER:
  https://us02web.zoom.us/j/86707734458
  Zoom Meeting ID: 867 0773 4458 or
  BY TELEPHONE: 1 669 900 9128, Enter Code 867 0773 4458#

ABSENT:

  Manager Rindge, Interim Police Chief Dreiling, City Clerk Chaney

1.  City Council Action Minutes

  Approved payment of Motions #1 and #2.

7.  Revisions to the Sick Leave Policy and the Family Medical Leave Act Policy to Include
  Supplemental Language Addressing Covid-19 Parameters during the Covid-19

  1. Accepted the supplemental language added to the Sick Leave Policy and The Family
  Medical Leave Act Policy and the Emergency Temperature Taking Policy to be

  2. Directed the City Manager to implement the supplemental procedures as mandated by
  Federal, State, and County Regulations for the benefit of its employees and their

  Reviewed and Approved.

9.  Conflict of Interest Code – Biennial Review

  Directed the City Clerk, in coordination with the City Attorney and City Manager, to review
  the City's Conflict of Interest Code to determine if changes to the Code are needed, and
  directed the City Manager to review and add all consultants.

  discussion and amendment, a motion to approve the extension of agreements with the

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES
June 9, 2020
 14.  Consideration and Possible Action to Pursue Joining the Los Angeles County Clean
  Power Alliance

  The following individuals addressed the City Council: Ann Nye, Connie Sullivan, Reggie
  Jue, Desiree Myers, Dawn Murdock, John Harbison, Christine McNamara, Bill Sewell, Jim
  Phelps, Camille Feldman, and Henry Bazak.

  ACTION: Moved by Councilmember Kao to direct staff to move forward with a
  Notice of Intent to obtain additional information from the Clean Power Alliance.
  Motion died for lack of second.

STAFF REPORTS

  i.  City Manager's Report
  None
  a. State of the Police Department – Oral Report
  None

MAYOR & CITY COUNCILMEMBERS' REPORTS

Councilmember Davidson reiterated his request for the City to engage a grant writer, requested future
agenda items including review the Mirlo Gate House, a potential Golf Tournament with the Golf
Club, and requested the police enforce the leaf blower ordinance.

Councilmember Lozzi requested enforcement of the leaf blower ordinance, requested that George
Allen field be added to a future agenda, and requested that the City Clerk and City Manager review
the Commission/Committee application period and process.

Councilmember Kao provided an update on recent meetings including the South Bay Cities Council
of Governments, police ad-hoc and the League of California Cities Public Safety and Policy
Committee, and provided an update on the Census self-reporting. He also requested future agenda
items for George Allen field opening for Little League and a potential review of the agreement, and
a potential town hall on race relations, potentially in partnership with the other Peninsula cities and
the school district.

Mayor Pro Tem Kemps requested a future agenda item for a grant writer, and a future agenda item
for Transparency.

Mayor McGowan reported on recent meetings with other cities for the re-opening process and recent
protests. He noted that he has been in conversation with the golf club regarding a potential
tournament, and is working with the Tennis and Golf clubs on the creation of a task-force to review
of operations of these facilities with a strategic goal to increase revenue for the City.

ADJOURNMENT to Tuesday, June 23, 2020 AT 6:30 PM

  NOES:  None
